title: Health Care
meta: Process improvement for Canadian health care organizations: better patient flow, shorter wait times and practical KPIs, built with staff and union partners.
h1: Better patient flow and clear KPIs, built with your front line
lead: Health care organizations must serve their communities while controlling capital and operating costs. We coach your teams to improve patient flow, productivity and service, with KPIs everyone from front line to executive understands.
intro: How do you improve care when budgets are tight?

Hospitals, clinics, long-term care homes and community health providers face rising demand, staffing pressure and fixed budgets. We know that improvement takes more than a boardroom conversation. Chmltech collaborates with your staff, physicians and union partners in relatable ways to improve patient flow, reduce wait times and remove work that adds no value for patients. We develop process measures that communicate your value from frontline to executive and act as your coaches in performance improvement. The result is a culture of continuous improvement that keeps delivering after the project ends.
signs: Wait times for appointments, procedures or beds keep growing
Patients are discharged late in the day, blocking new admissions
Staff spend too much time searching for supplies or information
Overtime and agency staffing costs are hard to control
Managers lack timely, trusted data on patient flow
challenges: Delays in one area, such as discharge or diagnostics, ripple through the system and lengthen waits for patients.
Clinical and support staff are stretched, so wasted steps and rework directly affect morale and patient experience.
Organizations must fulfil their duty to the communities they serve while reducing capital and operating expenses.
Change imposed from the top meets resistance. Lasting improvement needs staff and union partners involved from the start.
services: We define metrics for service levels, productivity, speed and quality, such as wait times and length of stay, and set a baseline to measure success.
We map the patient journey from referral or arrival to discharge, find the delays and work with teams to reduce wait times.
A thorough as-is analysis: process mapping, financial and operating data review, direct observation and a review of current management tools.
Observations of clinical and support work separate what adds value for patients from waste such as searching, waiting and duplicate documentation.
Change management with staff and unions
We assess change readiness and build a plan that involves staff and union partners, so your people drive and own the change.
We help leadership turn strategy into daily activities, using visual boards, huddles and practical automation of scheduling and reporting.

steps.label: Confirm medically ready
steps.text: On rounds, the physician confirms the patient is medically ready to go home.

steps.label: Write discharge order
steps.text: The discharge order and prescriptions are often written late in the day, after rounds and other urgent work, so the bed stays occupied.

steps.label: Page for the order
steps.text: Nurses page and re-page the physician for the order, then wait for it to come back.

steps.label: Prepare discharge meds
steps.text: Pharmacy fills the discharge prescriptions and arranges any transport.

steps.label: Discharge teaching
steps.text: Nursing explains medications, follow-up and warning signs.

steps.label: Ride home arranged
steps.text: Family confirms the ride home and any support at home.

steps.label: Clean and turn bed
steps.text: Environmental services cleans the room and bed management marks it ready.

steps.label: Admit next patient
steps.text: The next patient moves up from emergency or recovery.

before: Orders written late in the day

config.fix_title: Fixed: expected discharge date and a morning huddle
config.fix_text: An expected discharge date is set at admission and a short morning discharge huddle confirms who is going home today. Orders and prescriptions are written earlier, pharmacy prepares ahead, and beds free up in time for the next admission.

examples: Discharge planning on a medical unit
Most discharges happened late in the afternoon, leaving emergency patients waiting for beds.
Expected discharge dates and a morning huddle move more discharges earlier in the day.
Supply rooms in a community clinic
Nurses walked between rooms looking for supplies that were often out of stock.
Standardized supply locations and a simple reorder system keep items where and when staff need them.
Referrals were tracked on paper and phone calls, and patients were unsure when they would be seen.
A single digital referral queue gives staff a clear view of waits and lets them book patients sooner.
outcomes: Shorter wait times and smoother patient flow
Clear KPIs understood from front line to executive
More staff time for direct patient care
Better control of operating and overtime costs
Stronger collaboration between management, staff and unions
A sustained culture of continuous improvement

why.title: Why Chmltech for health care
why.text: We act as your coaches in performance improvement. We do not leave you with a report; we engage your people through every step.
points: We aim for a return of at least 3:1 on your investment. Before the project starts, we agree an ROI target with you and how it will be measured.
We work with your team and union partners in relatable ways, so changes are designed by the people who deliver care.
We look at people, management behaviour and use of technology as well as processes, to address the real causes of delays.
why.note: ROI targets are set for each engagement based on scope and baseline data. Actual results depend on scope, implementation and operating conditions.

faq: Do you work with unionized health care environments?
Yes. We involve union partners early and work collaboratively with staff, which builds trust and helps changes last.
Will this add work for already busy clinical staff?
We design sessions to fit around patient care and shift patterns. The aim is to remove wasted steps so staff have more time for patients, not less.
What kinds of health care organizations do you support?
We work with hospitals, clinics, long-term care homes, community health providers and health-related service organizations across Canada.
How do you measure improvement in health care?
We agree KPIs such as wait times, length of stay, throughput and staff time on direct care, set a baseline and track results against it and an agreed ROI target.
